checklist.intro: Mollie is our licensed payment provider. Its form uses business wording: that is normal, and it does not call your non-profit status into question. Here are the documents to prepare.

activity.meaning: What your association actually does and where the collected funds come from. Describe it in plain words: Mollie expects a description, not an NAF code.

bank.meaning: Bank details (RIB) in the association's name, with a French IBAN.

identity.meaning: An identity document (ID card or passport) for each declared beneficial owner, legal representative included: these are personal documents, not documents belonging to the association.

registration.link: Find my record on the Annuaire des Entreprises
registration.meaning: Your prefecture declaration receipt (récépissé de déclaration) or your JOAFE publication extract; for an association recognised as being of public utility, the recognition decree; in Alsace-Moselle, the extract from the association register of the judicial court.

stakeholders.meaning: The association's officers and beneficial owners: chair, treasurer, and anyone exercising effective control. For an association these are the board members, with their date of birth and address.

checklist.note: Depending on your case, Mollie may ask for additional documents, such as your statutes or the list of your officers.

info.intro: You are about to hand documents to a company you may never have heard of. Here is who Mollie is, why this step cannot be skipped, and what becomes of your documents.

documents.body: The documents you upload in the Mollie form go to Mollie alone. CommonLink does not receive them, does not store them and has no access to them: of this connection, the platform records only technical items - access tokens, your Mollie account identifier, the state of the connection and the address of your Mollie dashboard. Mollie encrypts data, meets the highest certification level for card payment security (PCI DSS) and acts as data controller under the GDPR.
documents.title: Where do your documents go?

funds.body: Donations are collected on your own Mollie account, opened in your association's name, then paid out to the bank account you register there. CommonLink never holds your funds and cannot move them.
funds.title: Where does the money go?

verify.body: Do not take our word for it: Mollie's licence is public, and its security commitments are published.
verify.registerLink: Mollie B.V. in the Dutch central bank's public register
verify.title: Check for yourself

who.body: Mollie B.V. is a Dutch payment provider, licensed as an electronic money institution by the central bank of the Netherlands (De Nederlandsche Bank) under the European payment services directive (PSD2). That licence is recorded in the central bank's public register and covers France, where Mollie operates under the European freedom to provide services.
who.title: Who is Mollie?

why.body: No payment institution may let an organisation collect funds without having verified its identity, its officers and the nature of its activity. That obligation falls on Mollie, not on your association: it is not a CommonLink requirement, and no serious platform can avoid it. CommonLink separately runs its own review of your file: the two checks are independent and add up to each other.
why.title: Why this verification is mandatory

welcome.title: Receive your donations
welcome.lead: To collect donations online, your association opens an account with Mollie, a licensed institution. We guide you through every screen: you will know what to prepare, what to answer, and where you stand.

faq.title: Your questions before you start
faq.hint: Read at your own pace, nothing is committed.

whyMollie.question: Why Mollie?
whyMollie.p1: Online donations go through a licensed institution. Ours is Mollie B.V., an electronic money institution licensed by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), client number F0038.
whyMollie.p2: The law requires Mollie to check who is behind every organisation that collects money: this is its anti-money-laundering obligation. That is why it asks you for documents.
whyMollie.p3: Its forms speak of "business", "registration" or "UBO": that is normal, and it does not call your non-profit status into question. "Business" = your association.

documents.question: Who sees my documents?
documents.p1: You upload your documents directly on Mollie's website. The documents you upload to Mollie are not passed on to us. We only receive the progress status of your file.
documents.p2: The documents you gave us for your CommonLink verification stay in your space: you can retrieve them to upload them to Mollie yourself.

cost.question: How much does it cost?
cost.p1: At Mollie, you will choose the "Charities and donations" category. Mollie may deduct onboarding fees from your first payout. Their amount is set by Mollie. Mollie does not publish it.
cost.p2: The €0.01 test payment is made by yourself; the money stays on your association's Mollie balance.

genuine.question: Is it the genuine website?
genuine.p1: Before typing anything, look at the address bar: it must show my.mollie.com. Otherwise, close the window and contact us.
genuine.p2: CommonLink will never ask for your Mollie password.

resume.question: Can I stop and come back later?
resume.p1: Yes. You can close the Mollie window at any time. Come back here and click "Resume my file": we take you back to your file at Mollie.

help.question: Need help?
help.p1: Book a guided video call: a member of the CommonLink team talks you through it while you fill in the form. You keep control of your screen and keyboard.
help.p2: CommonLink never asks for your password.
